title: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
claim: Prior methods either downsample the scene or score many precomputed instances; ours lets an agent actively search via multi-view tool calls.
layout: 3 panels: large left 'ours', two stacked right 'prior' panels; checklist device
description: A wide figure with a large shaded panel (a) on the left and two stacked white panels (b, c) on the right. Panel (a), 'Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding', shows an aerial textured city-scale 3D campus model with three camera frustums (black global, blue zoomed, orange oblique) pointing at it. Above it, an 'Urbex Agent' box connects to a 'Result' box and exchanges arrows with a 'Tools calling' box. A blue checklist reads 'End to end', 'Once inference', 'High quality views'. Panel (b), 'Regular Grounding Method', shows a sparse downsampled point cloud with a DownSampling → Model → Result flow and '50k points'. Panel (c), 'Ranking-based Grounding Method', shows three building crops with scores 0.98, 0.93, 0.88 and '1.3k instances need scoring'. The eye goes first to the large city render.
caption: Overview of \method{}. Unlike regular grounding methods that downsample city-scale point clouds or ranking-based methods that score many precomputed instances, \method{} formulates grounding as agentic spatial search. A VLM agent actively interacts with the scene through tool calls, moving between global, zoomed, and oblique views before committing the final target location.
abstract: City-scale 3D grounding is commonly formulated as candidate ranking, which requires precomputed instance proposals and becomes inefficient in large outdoor scenes. We propose Urbex, an agentic vision-language framework that instead casts grounding as active spatial search. Urbex represents a city-scale 3D scene as an interactive multi-view environment, allowing a VLM agent to query landmarks, zoom into local regions, render oblique views, and commit a grounded bounding box. We optimize this tool-use policy with reinforcement learning on CityRefer, using smooth localization rewards and lightweight shaping rewards for efficient exploration. Experiments show that Urbex achieves the best Hit@1 and IoU on CityRefer, supports candidate-free grounding without ground-truth boxes, and is substantially faster than the strongest city-scale ranking baseline. Zero-shot results on STPLS3D-Refer further indicate improved cross-scene robustness.
